title: Expiration duration adds no reliable nocturnal-cough prediction beyond standard spirometry in two NHANES surveys
abstract: We tested whether log spirometric forced expiratory time adds symptom information beyond standard lung-function measures and demographic/smoking adjustment. Frozen weighted logistic models trained in NHANES2007-2008 (3711 adults;214 cases) were evaluated in separately recruited NHANES2011-2012 (3690 adults;195 cases). The outcome was self-reported nocturnal dry cough over the preceding12months. Target Brier score was 0.04412788 without versus 0.04412244 with duration; delta -0.00000543, joint training-refit/target-PSU95% interval [-0.00016518,+0.00024089]. AUC delta was +0.000342. No reliable incremental predictive benefit was demonstrated. This is a negative incremental-value test, not evidence of equivalence or absence of airway physiology. Sequential prior survey exposure, few symptom cases, protocol-dependent duration, incomplete confounder adjustment and same-program transport limit interpretation.
